name: VRP overshoot short — IV>RV into an exhausted rally (4h perp)
rationale: ECONOMIC MECHANISM (the SHORT-side expression of the variance risk premium: when the options market prices a fat premium (dvol>>vol_realized) AND price has rallied into an overbought exhaustion, the calmer-than-priced window favors a mean-reversion DOWN, not up — so we take the short leg on a perp and collect funding if longs are paying. This is the sign-inverted counterpart to the long VRP harvest and only makes sense as a distinct cell because the entry crowding condition is an OVERBOUGHT rally, not a calm dip): a wide IV-over-RV gap means dealers are charging a variance premium to a retail flow overpaying for convexity (Deribit 2025); implied>>realized forecasts realized undershoots implied -> the coming window is calm, and a rally that overshot into overbought mean-reverts within that calm. Entry (short, direction -1): dvol above a fitted floor (premium present) AND vol_realized below a fitted ceiling (calm relative to implied) AND rsi above a fitted overbought floor (the rally is exhausted). With funding_rate wired, a short RECEIVES funding when the rate is positive (longs paying) — extra carry on the mean-reversion. Exit: rsi crosses down out of overbought (reversion paid) or stop/TP/time. DISCONFIRMER 1: if a plain overbought-RSI short (drop both vol legs) matches the deflated Sharpe, the VRP adds nothing and this is generic mean-reversion. DISCONFIRMER 2: if this and the long VRP harvest (hh-volatility-01) both clear on the same symbols, the IV>RV spread is not selecting direction — the RSI leg is doing all the work. HARD CAVEAT: ~148 DVOL points -> paper-only; short-perp adverse-selection and funding-sign risk make this the harder side.
catalyst: a variance premium into an overbought exhausted rally — a calm-window fade down
